issues.description: Regex `/\dm?s/i` is a loose over-approximation that can match non-time substrings (urls, strings, identifiers).
issues.detail: The pre-filter matches any digit followed by optional `m` and `s`, so values like `url(foo1s.png)`, `"abc1ms"`, or `--1ms-var` still enter the parser. Correctness is preserved because the authoritative valueParser runs after, but the looseness erodes the speedup and should be acknowledged or tightened (e.g. `\dm?s\b`).

issues.description: Name `HAS_TIME` overstates what the predicate decides; rename to reflect heuristic nature.
issues.detail: The constant is a cheap pre-filter, not a fact about the value. A name like `MAY_CONTAIN_TIME` or `LIKELY_HAS_TIME` separates the heuristic from the authoritative parser and prevents future maintainers from mistaking the regex for the source of truth on time tokens.

issues.description: Document the invariant tying the regex pre-filter to the valueParser contract.
issues.detail: The module now has two notions of "contains a time token" — the regex and the parser walk — with no comment stating that regex-fails implies no time token exists. A one-line comment naming this as a deliberate over-approximation and noting that future CSS time units must update both sites would protect the abstraction.

issues.description: No benchmark numbers or regression test pinning the early-return behaviour.
issues.detail: This is sold as a performance fix but ships without before/after measurements in the changeset and without a fixture that exercises the awkward cases (url(), custom properties with `ms`, quoted strings, vendor-prefixed properties). A single test locking in early-return equivalence with the prior implementation would close the audit.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously accepts this as a small, well-shaped performance patch: a cheap regex short-circuits the expensive valueParser call when no time-like token is present, preserving correctness because the authoritative parser still runs on candidates. Consensus concerns are all minor and non-blocking: the regex `/\dm?s/i` is a loose over-approximation, the name `HAS_TIME` overstates what it decides, and no comment documents the invariant linking the fast-path to the parser. The change ships without benchmark numbers or a regression test guarding the early-return. Verdict: land with light fixups — rename, add a one-line comment naming the heuristic, and ideally add a fixture covering url()/string/custom-property edge cases.
